title: Bennie Owen: OU's Longest-Tenured Football Coach (1905-1926)
question: How long did Bennie Owen coach Oklahoma football and what was his record?
answer: Bennie Owen coached the Oklahoma Sooners from 1905 through 1926, the longest tenure of any OU head coach, and went 122-54-16. His 1911, 1915 and 1918 teams went unbeaten, and Owen Field carries his name.
summary: Bennie Owen coached Oklahoma from 1905 to 1926, went 122-54-16, posted three unbeaten seasons and gave his name to Owen Field. Here is his story.
body: Before Wilkinson, Switzer or Stoops, there was Bennie Owen. He took over the Oklahoma program in 1905 and stayed on the sideline through the 1926 season, a 22-year run that is still the longest of any Sooner head coach. His OU record was 122 wins, 54 losses and 16 ties, which makes him one of only four coaches in school history with more than 100 victories.

Owen arrived in Norman with a winning résumé. He had been the quarterback on Fielding Yost's unbeaten Kansas team in 1899, then coached at Washburn and at Bethany College in Kansas. At Oklahoma he built three undefeated teams: 8-0 in 1911, 10-0 in 1915 and 6-0 in 1918. His Sooners also won Southwest Conference titles in 1915 and 1918 and a Missouri Valley title in 1920.

He was known for an open, attacking style. The College Football Hall of Fame calls him an early champion of the forward pass, and his 1914 team led the nation in scoring. Toughness was part of the legend too. Owen lost his right arm in a 1907 hunting accident, coached from his hospital bed for weeks, and was back traveling with the team a little over a month later.

After coaching, Owen served as OU's athletic director into the 1930s. The program he built gave the school the momentum to raise money for a permanent campus stadium, which went up in stages beginning in 1925, and its playing surface became Owen Field. In 1951 he was part of the first class inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame, a fitting honor for the coach who laid the foundation for everything that came after.
